items.title: Set up the project repo using the Claude Code CLI (your first CLI session)
items.concept: Claude Code CLI basics — install, auth, first prompt, first commit
items.sourceItem: Onboarding — learn the CLI before building the agents
items.goal: End the session with a new GitHub repo, Claude Code running in your terminal, and one commit that Claude Code made for you.
steps: Create an empty GitHub repo named aiml-signal-system. [done]
Clone it locally and cd into it. [done]
Install the Claude Code CLI and authenticate. [done]
Run `claude` in the repo and ask it to scaffold README + folders (agents/, data/, design/).
Ask Claude Code to make the first git commit, then push.
items.doneWhen: The repo on GitHub shows a README and folders, committed by a Claude Code session you drove.
items.notes: Repo, clone, CLI install + login all complete. Remaining: first scaffolding prompt + commit.

items.title: Have Claude Code build a minimal stateless 'echo' MCP server
items.concept: MCP 2026-07-28 stateless request/response (from today's lead item)
items.goal: Feel the stateless model firsthand: a tiny MCP server with one 'echo' tool, no session state, that any process instance can answer.
steps: In a new Claude Code session, ask it to create a minimal MCP server exposing one 'echo' tool on the 2026-07-28 stateless spec.
Ask it to explain, in comments, where state would have lived in the old stateful model.
Run it locally and call the tool twice; confirm no session is required between calls.
items.doneWhen: You can call the echo tool from a fresh connection with zero shared session state, and can explain why that's the point of the spec.
items.notes: Queued after hw-01. Good second CLI session.
